scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent friendship-email reading assessment with original questions, pending pedagogical validation

questions.q: What is Mara admitting by refusing the usual excuse that she was busy?
choices: She has not sent any photographs at all.
The silence reflects avoidance rather than a lack of time alone.
She has forgotten Jules's address.
Her archive work has prevented all communication.
questions.explanation: Mara recognises that she chose polished posts in place of meaningful contact.

questions.q: What does the sunset photograph illustrate?
choices: Her skill at recording beautiful views.
The importance of Bristol's waterfront.
A way to advertise the community archive.
An attractive response that concealed an uncomfortable truth.
questions.explanation: Mara used a sunset picture instead of answering whether she was happy.

questions.q: How does the archive challenge a simple idea of what a good memory should be?
choices: It accepts stories without requiring inspirational endings.
It asks contributors to prove every detail with documents.
It refuses to preserve disagreements between neighbours.
It allows only positive accounts of the city.
questions.explanation: Contributors can describe arguments or withhold recordings; the archive respects complexity.

questions.q: What does the contributor who refused to be recorded demonstrate?
choices: People cannot trust any archive to preserve material.
Written descriptions always contain more information.
Respect for a person can include accepting limits on what is recorded.
The community archive has no place for audio.
questions.explanation: The archive honours a request to keep only a written account of the room.

questions.q: Why does the retired shopkeeper's story stay with Mara?
choices: It explains why he had moved to the seaside.
He seeks recognition of a place's importance rather than sympathy or advice.
It proves that the shop sold better tea than others.
It prompts Mara to change her employer.
questions.explanation: The man wants someone to know the shop mattered without being offered consolation.

questions.q: What broader lesson does Mara draw from that interview?
choices: Friends should give one another practical advice immediately.
Memories matter only if they are recorded.
The archive should avoid interviewing people in grief.
Attentive listening may matter more than providing solutions.
questions.explanation: Mara concludes that attention is often more important than advice.

questions.q: Why does Mara hesitate before inviting Jules?
choices: The invitation could feel like a test of their friendship.
She is uncertain about the location of the archive event.
She wants Jules to deliver a public lecture.
The archive has already cancelled the evening.
questions.explanation: Mara wants the invitation not to become a measurement of whether the friendship still works.

questions.q: What does Mara acknowledge about an enjoyable evening together?
choices: It can necessarily repair a year of silence.
It makes ordinary conversations unnecessary.
It cannot automatically undo a year of superficial contact.
It would prove that neither friend has changed.
questions.explanation: Mara rejects the claim that one event can repair their neglected connection.

questions.q: Why does Mara allow Jules to attend without contributing?
choices: She needs another person to manage the recordings.
She wants company without imposing a performance or obligation.
Only trained archivists are permitted to contribute.
She expects Jules to pay the event costs.
questions.explanation: The invitation explicitly removes any expectation to take part formally.

questions.q: What tension shapes the closing invitation?
choices: The desire to share professional success and avoid disagreement.
The need to give Jules an inspiring personal lesson.
The wish to end the relationship without saying so.
The desire for renewed connection without turning it into another task.
questions.explanation: Mara wants space for uncertain, genuine friendship rather than managed closeness.
